source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use body weight alone for every antineoplastic agent, regardless of the regimen's prescribed dosing method.","B":"Estimate body surface area visually, because precise height and weight measurements are unnecessary for dosing.","C":"Calculate body surface area from verified measurements and apply the regimen's prescribed mg-per-square-meter amount.","D":"Convert every oncology dose to a fixed adult amount, because body-size-based dosing is no longer used in modern practice."}}
source_row.rationale: When a regimen is ordered in mg/m², the nurse calculates the dose from current BSA and the prescribed mg/m², while recognizing that organ function, toxicity, maximum doses and regimen-specific adjustments remain separate clinical considerations.
source_row.source_detail: Final guidance discusses dosage selection and optimization for oncology products and the need to use regimen- and patient-specific evidence rather than assuming one body-size metric guarantees optimal exposure. FDA final guidance, August 2024; current FDA page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: FDA — Optimizing Dosage for Oncologic Diseases
source_row.stem: An oncology regimen prescribes a medication dose in mg/m². Which nursing action correctly uses body surface area (BSA) dosing?
